review_method: Every scene judged from its contact board in qa/footage-candidate-boards/, then each intended pick re-checked against the provider slug before it was written here. Provider ranking was treated as an inspection order only. Three picks were reversed at the slug check: 32386531 is an industrial conveyor and not server racks, 13008924 is people colliding and not an airlock, and 5940166 is a teacher with students and not independent researchers.
policy: A scene is filled only when a candidate actually shows the required content. Where nothing fits, the scene is blocked with the reason recorded, rather than filled with an approximate frame.

selections.inspection_note: Two engineers at one shared display, one driving and one reviewing. The only frame in the set showing genuine joint review rather than a lone operator or an empty desk.

selections.reason: No live server infrastructure exists in this candidate set. The frame that looked like a motion pass through racks is an industrial conveyor system with red lights (32386531); the only other hardware shot is a hard drive being inserted into a storage enclosure (38496192). The rest are a video-editing timeline, a pedestrian underpass and a metal workshop. Filling this would misrepresent a conveyor belt as compute.

selections.inspection_note: Two people at a desk reading time-series and dashboard output on monitor and laptop. Closest available to plural observers watching a run; reads as an analytics review rather than a lab evaluation, so cut it short and let narration carry the specificity.
Operator leaning into a multi-monitor setup with green terminal text on the secondary screen. Delivers both halves of the brief: scrolling terminal output and a person deliberately watching it.
Fire department training ground: crews spraying into open air with no fire present. Unmistakably rehearsed rather than a real emergency, which is the whole point of the scene.
Sample rotator with tubes loaded and run time set on the panel. Shows a controlled run being configured rather than generic lab atmosphere.
Hands drawing and annotating a curve on a whiteboard with prior working still visible. Reads as scenario analysis being reworked, not a generic meeting at a board.
Tokyo towers shot from below. Conveys capital at scale with no legible corporate mark and no named transaction, unlike the branded alternatives in this set.
Two identical booth workstations side by side, one person in each, working separately but within arm's reach. The closeness of the frontier made literal and human.

selections.reason: No security operations centre. The set is a man on a phone at a podium, crypto and stock dashboards, a lone programmer in a red-lit room, a business meeting, and a 'hacker' scene whose monitor shows a Guy Fawkes mask on a video call. The last would be actively damaging: it imports an internet-meme image of hacking into a claim about real cyber extortion.

No network traffic analysis. Four of six are trading or crypto desks, one is a man on a phone, and the top-ranked frame is a man typing while holding a bank card, which would imply consumer payment fraud rather than incident response.

No server hall. Same empty pool as scene_002 — conveyor, hard drive, processor close-up — plus a laundry room with people dancing on a table and a crypto trading setup. Nothing here can carry a night-time server hall under defence.

No large-scale network activity. Three frames are crypto or stock dashboards, one is a code desk, one is a man reading a corporate KPI wall, and the remaining one is a rotating CGI geometric shape — a decorative graphic that visualises no real data. Using it would put a fabricated visualisation under an espionage claim.

selections.inspection_note: Mask, goggles and gloves at a microscope in natural lab light. The most credible PPE frame available; the alternatives are studio-lit gel backdrops that read as staged.
Gloved hands working plates inside a cabinet with the sash in frame. Genuine containment work rather than an open bench.

selections.reason: No controlled access to a secured facility. Ranked candidates are a person entering a train station, women bumping shoulders near glass doors, an empty hallway, two lab-analyser shots, and a woman entering a building signed for University of the Arts London. Nothing shows access being granted or restricted.

selections.inspection_note: One person at home absorbed in her phone in ordinary low light. Single subject, no event, no performance — the ordinariness is the point.
A row of people standing together, each looking down at their own handset. Literal reading of the brief; the crowd alternatives are all people pointing phones at one shared event.
Hands typing a document on a laptop with a coffee at the desk. Unglamorous office work carried out through software, no code-editor styling.

Textile worker handling output beside a running machine line with its own control panel. The human step and the automated step sit adjacent in one frame. Note the automation shown is industrial, not software — acceptable for the visual argument but worth checking against narration wording.

selections.reason: No data centre. Every candidate is an office block, a glass tower, or a logistics site: warehouse roofs with solar panels, an industrial park shot from a hot air balloon, an industrial area and car park. Presenting a distribution warehouse as a hyperscale data centre would be a factual misrepresentation of the shot.

No compute racks. The set is the hard drive insertion, a red bokeh light, a man scanning stock in a pallet warehouse, the same industrial conveyor, and two CGI abstractions (a circuit-board cityscape and a hexagonal surface). No hall of racks exists to concentrate.

selections.inspection_note: Power plant switchgear and insulators. Unmistakable electrical generation and distribution infrastructure, which is the dependency the scene names.

Drone view of the Budapest parliament building, read wide as an institution. Caveat for editorial: this is a national parliament, not an EU body, and Budapest is recognisable. Fine if narration is about legislatures generally; re-brief if the line is specifically about Brussels.

Clean EU flag on a pole, stars fully legible. Shortfall recorded honestly: there is no official building in frame, so this delivers 'the EU' but not 'flags outside a building'. Every candidate that had a building had Italian flags at Milan station or Swiss flags at Bundesplatz, both of which would have been wrong.

selections.reason: No European formal chamber. The set is an ornate ballroom ceiling, two museum interiors, an aerial of the Utah State Capitol, a generic conference room, and a masked press conference beside a US flag. The two that are genuinely legislative are American.

selections.inspection_note: Suited officials in conversation in a corridor with more of them in the background. The only frame in the set that is institutional rather than an airport concourse.

selections.reason: Nothing measured or monitored. The processor close-up shows compute but no measurement; the rest are a video-editing timeline, crypto dashboards, a code desk and a backlit keyboard. No utilisation, telemetry or capacity readout appears anywhere in the set.

selections.inspection_note: Three colleagues working through a document together, actively disagreeing over it. The friction suits 'obligations' better than a calm read-through.

Colleagues collaborating over a laptop at a library desk. Chosen over the higher-ranked frame from the same shoot because that one is a teacher with students — a hierarchy the brief's 'independent' explicitly rules out.
Two researchers at a lab bench with tubes and microscopes, one walking the other through the work. Reads as a university lab passing on shared technique.
A code editor open on a personal laptop with hands on the keys. One developer, own machine, actually editing rather than browsing.

selections.reason: No access control or centralised monitoring. The set is an empty office, a man on a phone, two crypto dashboards, a camera device screen, and the same masked video-call frame rejected at scene_010.

selections.inspection_note: Two people jointly reading a document in a neutral office. Held distinct from scene_029 by staging: this is a quiet two-hander read, that one is a three-way argument.
Gowned and masked operator working through automated analysers. Chosen over the soldering frame, which shows assembly rather than evaluation — the brief asks for testing, not building.
Panel table with desk microphones and members in discussion. No flag or national marker, so it reads as an evaluation panel rather than a specific institution.
One person at the microscope inspecting while a second writes on a clipboard. Inspection, measurement and the recording of it all present in a single frame.
Hands working through a thick paper stack beside ring binders. Record-keeping in motion, with no document type legible — the alternative had a divorce decree readable on screen.
A full pedestrian crossing mid-flow. Ordinary people, ordinary movement, faces visible, no event to explain.
Commuters streaming out of a metrobus stop beside moving traffic. Everyday transit at human scale, unbranded, no station signage dominating.
Mother and child resting together on a sofa with no device anywhere in frame. The 'away from the technology' condition is met literally, which most of this set fails.

Empty white corridor receding to a vanishing point. Works as the machine's corridor by architecture and emptiness; note it is a metaphor, not literal server infrastructure, since none exists in this pool.
Close-up of a processor and memory slots. Concentrated compute in the most literal available sense — the silicon itself, since no data centre footage was obtainable.
Mexico City downtown at dusk from above, sprawling to the horizon. Genuine dusk light and no legible signage, unlike the branded skylines and the Las Vegas strip in this set.
A face lit only by its own screen in a dark room. One person, one display, closing intimacy; he is on a call, which is a minor distraction but does not break the read.
